title: BLOCK: Resolve Decision 4 — static-deps response scope (whole-repo vs per-component)
description: Blocking pre-implementation task for add-testaruda-adapter (openspec/changes/add-testaruda-adapter/design.md Decision 4). Decide whether the adapter's static-deps response returns the whole-repo affected set (option b) or is scoped per-component (option a). Option (a) requires cross-component dependency edges the adapter protocol has no command to hand over; option (b) matches titi's existing DG-04 computation but means testaruda's TIA-COMP-003 is intentionally not exercised for adapter-owned components. Needs testaruda maintainer decision or AdapterIO/composability-engine source review. Spec implication: a testaruda-side spec clarification may be required.
close_reason: RESOLVED: Whole-repo (option b) confirmed against testaruda v0.2.3 (commit 34e8db6). store.rs hardcodes component='default' for all adapter data (store_discovered_tests, store_static_deps); TIA-COMP-008 (parallel per-component selection) is specified but not implemented. engine.rs runs one flat Ascent program with test_comp used only for fallback scoping, not per-component adapter queries. The Julia adapter change (add-julia-adapter-via-testimonial Decision 5) poses the identical scoping question and notes whole-repo discover composes with testaruda's existing single-store architecture. Caveat: if testaruda later implements TIA-COMP-008, adapters spanning multiple logical components may need re-scoping — shared open question tracked by the Julia adapter change. Updated add-testaruda-adapter design.md Decision 4 and proposal.md; CLI-19 TIA-COMP note updated.

title: BLOCK: Resolve Decision 2 — adapter process-lifetime model
description: Blocking pre-implementation task for add-testaruda-adapter (openspec/changes/add-testaruda-adapter/design.md Decision 2). Confirm against testaruda's actual AdapterIO implementation (commit e8fad5b / v0.2.0) that a single long-lived adapter process per testaruda invocation is supported. If testaruda spawns a fresh process per command, the 30s cold-graph-build budget (DG-08) is paid multiple times per invocation and the adapter is unusably slow on large monorepos. Spec CLI-19 currently asserts the long-lived model; this task confirms or revises that. Resolution: spike against testaruda's AdapterIO source, record outcome in design.md, update CLI-19 if needed.
close_reason: RESOLVED: Long-lived adapter process model confirmed against testaruda v0.2.3 (commit 34e8db6) src/adapter.rs. AdapterIO::spawn performs handshake once and holds the Child; all subsequent commands reuse the same process via send(); kill() consumes self at end. main.rs spawns one adapter per testaruda invocation and issues multiple commands. Per-command spawning is not how the current core operates. Updated add-testaruda-adapter design.md Decision 2 and proposal.md; CLI-19 hedge removed.

title: S4: Resolve InTitiContext contradiction between RS-04 and SG-04
description:
Cross-capability contradiction between RS-04 and SG-04:

- solution-generation SG-04: unconditionally states that generated solution includes InTitiContext=true for all builds initiated from the transient solution
- reference-swap RS-04: states that when no swaps occur, SwapResult.msbuildContext has inTitiContext=false

SG-04's globalProperties are meant to flow from SwapResult.msbuildContext — the exact object RS-04 describes. So for 'titi open' on a project whose dependencies have no local source available (a plausible ordinary case), SG-04 requires InTitiContext=true while RS-04 requires false.

Add a conditional to one of these, or define the relationship precisely enough to show which wins.
close_reason: Fixed: SG-04 now conditional on swap result, with two scenarios matching RS-04's contract

title: S2: Fix CLI-08 TFM compatibility rule — non-empty intersection is wrong; should be superset
description:
In CLI-08 (cli/spec.md) the requirement states: '(2) its target framework set has a non-empty intersection with each consumer's target framework set.'

This is incorrect. A consumer that multi-targets net8.0;net9.0 needs the referenced project to support BOTH TFMs — if the candidate only supports net9.0, MSBuild will fail on the consumer's net8.0 leg. The correct rule is that the candidate's TFM set must be a SUPERSET of the consumer's TFM set.

This also affects reference-swap RS-01 which references the same compatibility concept but never states its own algorithm.
close_reason: Fixed: CLI-08 TFM rule now uses 'superset' instead of 'non-empty intersection'

title: S3: Specify versionPolicy=FORCE — declared in RS-01 and CF-02 but has no defined behaviour
description:
versionPolicy=FORCE is declared in RS-01 (reference-swap/spec.md) and CF-02 (configuration/spec.md) as a valid value alongside STRICT and SEMVER_COMPATIBLE, but has ZERO requirements or scenarios anywhere in the nine spec files.

An implementer has a named, user-facing policy value with no defined behaviour. We need to decide:
- Which safety checks does FORCE bypass? (version, TFM, cycle, transitive floor?)
- How does it interact with the overrides bypass set that RS-01 defines for the same purpose?
- Document the behaviour with scenarios.
close_reason: Fixed: FORCE policy behavior defined in RS-01 (bypasses all safety checks except NO_LOCAL_SOURCE) with two scenarios

title: S1: Fix DG-04 Completeness invariant direction — the formal invariant asserts the wrong reachability direction
description:
In dependency-graph/spec.md, DG-04 states: 'For every project P in the graph, if P is reachable via dependency edges from any project in directlyAffected, then P SHALL appear in either directlyAffected or transitivelyAffected.'

This is backwards. Dependency edges go from a project TO its dependencies. So 'reachable via dependency edges from X' means X's upstream dependencies. But transitivelyAffected contains downstream DEPENDENTS of directlyAffected projects.

The invariant should say: 'if P is reachable from a directly affected project by following dependency edges in reverse (i.e. P is a transitive dependent of a directly affected project), then P SHALL appear in either directlyAffected or transitivelyAffected.'

The clarifying sentence 'No downstream dependent...' was added post-review but the formal invariant text itself is still provably wrong against the spec's own DG-02 worked example.
close_reason: Fixed: DG-04 Completeness invariant now uses correct direction (reachable by following dependency edges in reverse)

title: S12: Fix error code naming — E009 and E008 used for semantically unrelated conditions
description:
Two name/usage mismatches in the error taxonomy:

1. **E009 = CONFIG_INVALID** — Used in configuration for missing/malformed config fields, but ALSO used in domain-model DM-02 for an invalid SemanticVersion string (e.g. 'latest'). These are unrelated semantic domains — a config loading error is different from a project parsing error.

2. **E008 = GIT_NOT_AVAILABLE** — Name implies 'git executable not found on PATH'. Actual uses: no .git root found (DG-01 — git IS present) and git version below 2.25 minimum (CF-08 — git IS present). The literal 'git not available' scenario is never specified under any code.
close_reason: Fixed: E008 renamed to GIT_ENVIRONMENT_ERROR; E009 usage clarified in DX-02 note

title: S10: Reconcile hardcoded .titi/ paths with configurable cache.directory
description:
CF-03 states cache.directory is configurable (default .titi/) and is 'the root artifact directory for ALL titi-generated files.' But every other capability hardcodes .titi/ instead of using the config value:

- graph-cache: .titi/graph.cache, .titi/graph.cache.tmp (dozens of occurrences)
- dependency-graph DG-09: .titi/graph.cache.lock
- solution-generation: .titi/solutions/..., .titi/solutions/<name>.fingerprint.edn
- cli: CLI-01, CLI-03, CLI-04 all hardcode .titi/

Either make all paths configurable via config value, or scope down CF-03's 'ALL' claim.
close_reason: Fixed: CF-03 scoped down to precise claim; all specs now reference cache.directory; added path-convention notes to cli, graph-cache, solution-generation specs

title: S11: Add cross-reference between DG-09 lock protocol and GC-08 atomic write — or consolidate
description:
Two specs describe overlapping write-protocol mechanics for .titi/graph.cache with no cross-reference between them:

- dependency-graph DG-09: Full lock-file state machine (UNLOCKED -> ACQUIRED -> WRITING -> RENAMED -> UNLOCKED) with PID-liveness-based stale-lock detection and per-state crash recovery
- graph-cache GC-08: Atomic tmp-file-then-rename protocol with its own 'Concurrency Note' about lock-free readers — never mentions the lock file from DG-09

Also sits awkwardly with OpenSpec's 'single purpose per capability' convention — cache concurrency belongs with graph-cache, not dependency-graph.
close_reason: Fixed: Added cross-references both ways between DG-09 (lock protocol) and GC-08 (atomic write)

title: S13: Fix VN-07 idempotency postcondition — falsified by VN-08 feed-dependent fallback
description:
VN-07 guarantees Idempotency: 'Running the algorithm twice on the same graph state and changeset inputs SHALL produce an identical version plan.'

But VN-08's 'Baseline feed unreachable' scenario makes BumpClassification depend on live feed reachability: unreachable -> treat as BREAKING. Two runs with identical inputs but different feed reachability produce different version plans.

Fix options:
1. Exclude feed-dependent baseline acquisition from the idempotency guarantee explicitly, or
2. Define feed reachability as part of the deterministic 'graph state' input (e.g. cache the first successful baseline fetch)
close_reason: Fixed: VN-07 idempotency postcondition now excludes feed-dependent baseline acquisition with explicit caveat

title: S5/S6: Reconcile RetainedReason vs ErrorCode overlap — NO_LOCAL_SOURCE and unused error codes
description:
Two related issues:

**S5 — NO_LOCAL_SOURCE collision:**
- RS-01: 'NO_LOCAL_SOURCE is informational only and is never bypassable'
- DX-02: E005 | NO_LOCAL_SOURCE | Aggregatable (first-class TitiError)

Decide: does a RetainedReason.NO_LOCAL_SOURCE outcome also produce a TitiError E005? Or are the two names an unrelated collision?

**S6 — Unused error codes:**
E003 (VERSION_MISMATCH), E004 (TFM_INCOMPATIBLE), E005 (NO_LOCAL_SOURCE), E010 (BUILD_FAILED), E011 (TEST_FAILED) have ZERO owning scenarios.

E010/E011 are especially concerning: there is no  or  command anywhere. Either these error codes are leftover from an earlier design and should be removed, or the spec set is missing a / capability.
close_reason: Fixed: Added note in DX-02 clarifying RetainedReason vs ErrorCode relationship; E010/E011 marked as reserved

title: S9: Add scenarios for 3 of 4 override bypass values that have no coverage
description:
RS-01 declares  can contain any of VERSION_MISMATCH, TFM_INCOMPATIBLE, CYCLE_PREVENTION, or TRANSITIVE_FLOOR_UNSATISFIED. Only CYCLE_PREVENTION has a scenario (RS-03).

Add scenarios for overriding a version mismatch, a TFM incompatibility, and a transitive floor violation. RS-06 (Transitive Floor Management) doesn't mention the override mechanism at all despite RS-01 listing that value as bypassable.
close_reason: Fixed: Added override scenarios for VERSION_MISMATCH, TFM_INCOMPATIBLE, and cross-ref to RS-06 for TRANSITIVE_FLOOR_UNSATISFIED

title: S7/S8: Account for bundles in versioning algorithm and domain model
description:
**S7:** The cascading-bump algorithm (VN-07) operates uniformly over 'changed packable projects' using ApiCompat assembly diffing. But bundles (metapackages) set  and produce no assembly — BN-01 explicitly states bundle versioning is 'based on changes to the bundle's externally visible dependency contract, not on assembly-level API comparison.' VN-07 has no exception, branch, or cross-reference for this.

**S8:** The domain model (DM-01) has no field to identify a bundle/metapackage project. The bundles capability (lint, check, update) and the carve-out needed from VN-07 both depend on identifying such projects programmatically. Add a field (e.g.  or ).
close_reason: Fixed: VN-07 now has bundle exception and cross-ref to bundles spec; DM-01 now has isMetapackage field
